question: An operations team must summarise several thousand short product blurbs every night, and the summaries get only a light human check. Which two factors should drive the tier choice? Select two.
options: A) How long each finished summary turns out to be, because length is what separates the tiers.
B) The reasoning depth the hardest problem anywhere in the company would need, as a safety margin.
C) The allowance the run consumes, because this same job repeats every single night of the week.
D) Whether the deepest tier appears on their plan at all, since availability settles the whole matter.
E) The throughput needed each night, because the volume makes speed per item a real constraint.
correct_answers: C) The allowance the run consumes, because this same job repeats every single night of the week.
E) The throughput needed each night, because the volume makes speed per item a real constraint.
explanations: Incorrect. Output length is set by the request, not by the tier, so it tells you nothing about which tier to pick.
Incorrect. Sizing for an unrelated hardest-case task overspends depth and quota on work that is simple and lightly reviewed.
Correct. A nightly repeat multiplies the allowance the job consumes, so recurring cost is a legitimate driver of the decision.
Incorrect. Availability is not the question; suitability for the task on cost, speed and quality is.
Correct. Thousands of items a night makes speed per item a genuine constraint, which is a core input to tier choice.
